label: Design

template_kind.description: Optional catalogue role: a reusable screen layout or a design-token system. Ordinary designs need neither.

description.description: A short description of what this design or template is for.

review.title: Review
review.description: Where review stands. Written only by designs.request_review, designs.approve and designs.request_changes; approved_rev is the revision an approval covers, and editing the design returns it to draft.

cites.description: Ids of the approved designs this one is built from. A template is CITED, never copied: a copy drifts the moment the original changes, and afterwards nothing can say which screens drifted. It is the same argument a panel makes for citing a metric rather than carrying its own SQL.

generated_by.description: The actor or model that emitted this spec. Null when a person authored it directly. Written by whatever files the design, because a platform whose thesis is provenance cannot have its generated work claim a human author.

sources.description: What the spec was derived from, as object ids. When one of them revises, this design is stale — the same mechanism a diagram generated from files already uses.

spec.title: Screens
spec.description: The design itself, declarative and never markup. An agent emits screens and the role of each element; the renderer draws them. Markup emitted by an agent cannot be diffed, cannot be reviewed as a proposal, and cannot be rendered without a sandbox - which is the same reason a panel is a mark plus a binding rather than authored SQL.

dx.description: Inside a container: shift from where the layout places it, in device pixels. Ignored when x and y are set.

dy.description: Inside a container: shift from where the layout places it, in device pixels. Ignored when x and y are set.

textStyle.description: Font-size token path, such as font.size.body. fontSize overrides this link.

cites.description: Provenance: a token path or component reference, checked against the resolved palette. This does not set paint or typography; use tone/color and textStyle/fontSize for those. A palette match verifies the citation only, not visual conformance.

tone.description: Which role in the palette this element plays. The renderer resolves it through the token set, so one token change restyles every element playing that role - the reason tokens exist at all.

color.description:
A colour token path from this design's palette — `color.accent`, `color.surface`, whatever the system defines — or a hex literal like `#ff00cc`. Wins over `tone` when both are set.

A token is the better thing to say, and a role better still: both follow the system when the system moves, and a literal follows nothing. It is allowed because sometimes the colour you need is not in the palette yet; it is reported as off-palette wherever the design is summarised, because a colour that cannot follow the system is drift whatever it looks like.

src.description: Asset id or https URL for an image. Absent draws a placeholder, which is honest about there being no picture yet rather than inventing one.

goto.description: Screen id this navigates to when clicked. This is how a prototype is click-through without a line of model-written JavaScript: the spec names a destination and the renderer owns the behaviour.

layout.description: Lay children out in a flex row or column instead of absolutely. This is what makes a design responsive: the container reflows, rather than every box carrying a coordinate that is only right at one width.

children.description: Children laid out by this element. One level deep on purpose — a recursive schema is a bet on how the generation API handles $ref, and a row of leaves covers most of what a screen needs.

tokens.description: Design tokens in the W3C DTCG shape - each entry is {$value, $type}, keyed by path (color.accent, radius.md). This is the ratified-definition layer for design, and it is a published standard rather than a private format: the same file is what design tools and token build tools already read. An element cites a token path, and a citation that does not resolve is off-system.

_note: Graph-backed on purpose. A design is an instance that gets proposed and revised like a dashboard, not a definition with its own lifecycle like a metric. The template/instance split is expressed by citation and `state`, not by a second store.
